title: Correlated Subquery with EXISTS
realWorldScenario: The support operations team wants a list of customers who have at least one refunded order.
questionStatement: Write a query using `EXISTS` to find all customers from `customers` who have at least one order with a corresponding record in the `refunds` table. Return `customers.id`, `customers.name`, and `customers.city`, sorted by `id` ascending.
starterCode:
-- Customers with at least one refund using EXISTS
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.name,
  c.city
FROM customers c
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM orders o
  JOIN refunds r ON o.id = r.order_id
  WHERE o.customer_id = c.id
)
ORDER BY c.id ASC;
hints: Correlate the subquery to the outer table using WHERE o.customer_id = c.id.
EXISTS only checks for the existence of rows, so SELECT 1 is standard convention.

testCases.description: Verify customers with recorded refunds (Customer 1 had order 110 refunded)
